headline: QuEra reports an MHS-enabled, AI-developed laser controller recovered 99.3% of testbed disturbances
summary: Anthropic's Aug 27 announcement opened an early preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a model-agnostic device interface with standardized discovery, state/procedure metadata and read/write controls. QuEra's same-day partner report describes using MHS and Claude to develop a controller for laser recovery on a dedicated, human-bounded quantum-computing testbed. QuEra reports 695 successful on-target recoveries in 700 induced trials (99.3%) across seven disturbance classes and automatic recovery of all 43 spontaneous mode hops observed during several weeks of testing. The AI-developed relock controller is a deterministic standalone script with AI out of the loop at runtime; a separate tuning workflow remains AI-in-the-loop. These are first-party partner results, not independently replicated or evidence of live fleet deployment.
